chapter.overview: This chapter details the architecture and operational mechanics of an AI tutor system, beginning with its limitations regarding factual accuracy despite linguistic fluency. It covers the training pipeline involving parameter adjustment via distinct datasets (training, validation, test) to prevent data leakage, alongside internal transformer mechanics like tokenization, causal attention masks, and positional encoding. The text explains optimization processes including loss functions, backpropagation, and regularization techniques such as dropout and early stopping. Post-training strategies are addressed through weight quantization for memory efficiency and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for context augmentation. Finally, the chapter establishes a dual-evaluation framework separating retrieval metrics (recall/precision) from answer generation quality, emphasizing protocols for handling conflicting information and uncertainty.

source_context.text: An artificial intelligence tutor answers questions about a collection of course documents. The tutor uses a language model to generate explanations, but fluent wording does not guarantee factual accuracy. During training, the language model adjusts its parameters using examples from a training dataset. A separate validation dataset supports model selection and the choice of training settings. A held-out test dataset measures performance after those choices have been made. These datasets must be separated carefully: if passages from the same source appear in both training and testing, the measured performance can overstate the model's ability to handle unfamiliar material. Dataset size alone does not establish dataset quality.
